Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Joseph Butler (author, Wikidata Q218322), died 1752; Howard Malcolm (editor, Wikidata Q16227445), died 1879. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Butler, Joseph, 1692-1752; Malcolm, Howard, 1799-1879 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The analogy of religion, natural and revealed ..., Philadelphia : J.B. Lippincott, 1876, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/analogyofrel1876butl. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 72%, 93%, 85% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Howard Malcolm, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
